guideline: Participants were asked to: (1) evaluate whether the article body was written by a human or an artificial intelligence, (2) rate confidence on a 5-point Likert scale, and (3) label whether the article had any distracting language or factual errors.
Participants judged human vs AI origin, confidence level, and error types (language errors, factual errors).

Participants were firstly asked to evaluate whether they believed the article body to be written by a human or an artificial intelligence. Subsequently, participants had to rate their confidence on a 5-point Likert scale from completely unsure (1) to completely sure (5). Finally, participants were asked to label whether the article had any distracting language or factual errors.

changes_made.explanation: Removed duplicate guideline entries and kept the most concise version. Removed 'fluency' from criteria as it was only mentioned in related work discussion, not as an explicit evaluation criterion in this study.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on evaluating GPT-3's ability to generate Danish news articles through human detection experiments and machine classification. The main NLG task is news article generation in Danish. Automatic metrics were used for evaluating the detection classifiers, though these are not traditional NLG quality metrics. The human evaluation was well-structured with clear criteria. The BERT model was used as a detector, not as an LLM judge for quality assessment.
